final_proof:
Proof. Fix \(p\) with \(1\le p<\infty\), and use the standard definition

\[
\ell^p=\left\{x=(x_n)_{n\ge1}\in\mathbb R^{\mathbb N}:\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}|x_n|^p<\infty\right\}.
\]

For sequences \(x=(x_n)\) and \(y=(y_n)\), pointwise addition means \((x+y)_n=x_n+y_n\). A scalar \(a\in\mathbb R\) is identified with the constant sequence \((a,a,\ldots)\), so pointwise multiplication gives the scalar multiplication \((a\cdot x)_n=ax_n\). We first verify that these operations are closed on \(\ell^p\).

For nonnegative \(u,v\), convexity of the function \(t\mapsto t^p\) gives

\[
\left(\frac{u+v}{2}\right)^p\le \frac{u^p+v^p}{2},
\]

and hence \((u+v)^p\le 2^{p-1}(u^p+v^p)\). Therefore, if \(x,y\in\ell^p\), the triangle inequality in \(\mathbb R\) yields, for every \(n\),

\[
|x_n+y_n|^p\le (|x_n|+|y_n|)^p\le 2^{p-1}(|x_n|^p+|y_n|^p).
\]

Summing these inequalities gives

\[
\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}|x_n+y_n|^p\le 2^{p-1}\left(\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}|x_n|^p+\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}|y_n|^p\right)<\infty.
\]

Thus \(x+y\in\ell^p\). If \(a\in\mathbb R\) and \(x\in\ell^p\), then

\[
\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}|ax_n|^p=|a|^p\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}|x_n|^p<\infty,
\]

where the equality also covers \(a=0\). Hence \(a\cdot x\in\ell^p\). The zero sequence \(0=(0,0,\ldots)\) belongs to \(\ell^p\), and if \(x\in\ell^p\), then \(-x=(-x_n)\in\ell^p\) because \(\sum|-x_n|^p=\sum|x_n|^p\). Thus the proposed operations, zero vector, and additive inverses all remain in \(\ell^p\).

It remains to verify the vector-space laws. Let \(x,y,z\in\ell^p\) and \(a,b\in\mathbb R\). For every \(n\ge1\), the field laws in \(\mathbb R\) give

\[
\begin{aligned}
(x+y)_n&=x_n+y_n=y_n+x_n=(y+x)_n,\\
((x+y)+z)_n&=(x_n+y_n)+z_n=x_n+(y_n+z_n)=(x+(y+z))_n,\\
(x+0)_n&=x_n+0=x_n,\\
(x+(-x))_n&=x_n-x_n=0,\\
(a\cdot(x+y))_n&=a(x_n+y_n)=ax_n+ay_n=(a\cdot x+a\cdot y)_n,\\
((a+b)\cdot x)_n&=(a+b)x_n=ax_n+bx_n=(a\cdot x+b\cdot x)_n,\\
((ab)\cdot x)_n&=(ab)x_n=a(bx_n)=(a\cdot(b\cdot x))_n,\\
(1\cdot x)_n&=1x_n=x_n.
\end{aligned}
\]

Two sequences are equal exactly when all their corresponding coordinates are equal. Consequently the displayed coordinatewise identities prove commutativity and associativity of addition, the zero and inverse laws, both distributive laws, compatibility of scalar multiplication with multiplication in \(\mathbb R\), and the scalar identity law. These are precisely the vector-space axioms. Therefore \((\ell^p,+,\cdot)_{\mathbb R}\) is a vector space.

If the convention for p-sequence spaces also includes \(p=\infty\), the same conclusion holds for \(\ell^\infty\): from \(|x_n+y_n|\le |x_n|+|y_n|\) one obtains \(\sup_n|x_n+y_n|\le\sup_n|x_n|+\sup_n|y_n|\), and \(\sup_n|ax_n|=|a|\sup_n|x_n|\); the coordinatewise verification of the axioms is unchanged.
